note: Curated short activities for older adults: 5 trivia, 4 story, 7 memory. `answer` is an integer INDEX into `options` (trivia/story only, same order in every locale). `tags` are internal (interest matching) and never shown. Locale-aware: *_en fields are used when the senior's locale is en and fall back to the Chinese field. No scoring, no diagnostic content.

activities.title: 油锅着了火
activities.prompt: 炒菜的时候油锅着了火，第一步该做什么？
activities.prompt_en: The oil in your wok catches fire while you are cooking. What should you do first?
options_en: Throw a basin of water on it
Put the lid on the pan
Carry the pan over to the sink
activities.explanation: 油比水轻，泼水会让热油溅起来，火更大；盖上锅盖，火没了空气，一会儿就灭。
activities.explanation_en: Oil is lighter than water, so water makes the hot oil splash and the flames grow. With the lid on, the fire has no air and soon goes out.
activities.wrong_hint: 这个法子有点险：油遇水会溅得更凶。
activities.wrong_hint_en: That one is a bit risky. Have another look.

activities.title: 冬天屋里生炉子
activities.prompt: 冬天在屋里用煤炉取暖，最要紧的是留什么？
activities.prompt_en: When a coal stove heats the room in winter, what matters most to leave?
options_en: Keep every door and window shut tight
Leave a little ventilation
Add another quilt
activities.explanation: 煤在屋里烧不透，会出一氧化碳，看不见也闻不着；窗户留一条缝，屋里透透气，人就安全。
activities.explanation_en: Coal burning indoors gives off carbon monoxide, which you can neither see nor smell. Leaving a gap at the window lets the air move through, and that keeps people safe.
activities.wrong_hint: 这一条关系到安全，差一点都不行。
activities.wrong_hint_en: This one is about safety. Please choose again.

activities.title: 白天最短的一天
activities.prompt: 一年里头，白天最短的是哪个节气前后？
activities.prompt_en: Around which solar term is the day shortest in the year?
options_en: Summer Solstice
Winter Solstice
Start of Autumn
activities.explanation: 冬至这天太阳照得最偏南，白天最短；过了冬至，白天就一天天长回来。
activities.explanation_en: At the Winter Solstice the sun sits furthest south, so the day is shortest. After it, daylight grows a little longer each day.
activities.wrong_hint: 是冷起来以后的那个节气。
activities.wrong_hint_en: Think again — it is the solar term that arrives as the cold sets in.

activities.title: 饺子浮起来了
activities.prompt: 煮饺子的时候，饺子都浮起来了，一般说明什么？
activities.prompt_en: While boiling dumplings, they all float to the top. What does that usually mean?
options: 差不多熟了，再煮一小会儿
皮已经破了，赶紧捞出来
options_en: They are far from done and need a long boil
They are nearly done — give them a little longer
The skins have split, so fish them out quickly
activities.explanation: 饺子受热以后，馅里的气把它托起来；浮起来再煮一小会儿，皮和馅就都熟透了。
activities.explanation_en: As dumplings heat up, steam inside lifts them to the surface. Once they float, a short extra boil cooks the skin and the filling through.
activities.wrong_hint: 浮起来是好事，说明时候到了。
activities.wrong_hint_en: No need to hurry — floating is a good sign. Have another look.

activities.title: 几种药一起吃
activities.prompt: 家里几种药想一起吃，最稳妥的做法是什么？
activities.prompt_en: You want to take several medicines at the same time. What is the safest thing to do?
options: 照着说明书自己配着吃
options_en: Follow the leaflets and work it out yourself
Ask a doctor or pharmacist first
Space them ten minutes apart and that is fine
activities.explanation: 不同的药一起吃，药性可能互相打架；让医生或者药师看一眼，比自己在家猜稳当。
activities.explanation_en: Different medicines can work against each other. Having a doctor or pharmacist look at them is steadier than guessing at home.
activities.wrong_hint: 这件事，最好问问懂行的人。
activities.wrong_hint_en: This is one to check with someone who knows medicines.

activities.title: 那台缝纫机
activities.story: 那台缝纫机，是我妈结婚时的嫁妆。白天她要上班，要做饭，只有等一家人都睡下了，才把缝纫机搬到灯底下。嗒嗒嗒，嗒嗒嗒，一件小褂子常常要缝到半夜。第二天早上，我就穿着新褂子去上学。
activities.story_en: That sewing machine was my mother's dowry when she married. In the daytime she worked and cooked; only when the whole family was asleep did she move the machine under the lamp. Tick-tick-tick, tick-tick-tick — one little jacket often took her half the night. The next morning I went off to school wearing it.
activities.prompt: 母亲为什么总要等大家都睡了，才踩缝纫机？
activities.prompt_en: Why did she always wait until everyone was asleep before she started sewing?
options_en: The ticking would wake the family
She could not find the thread in the daytime
The lamp was brighter at night
activities.explanation: 缝纫机一踩就嗒嗒响，夜里安静，声音传得远；等大家睡熟了再做，是怕吵着人。
activities.explanation_en: The machine ticks loudly, and at night the quiet carries the sound. She waited until everyone was sound asleep so as not to disturb them.
activities.wrong_hint: 故事里的那个声音，给了您一点提示。
activities.wrong_hint_en: The sound in the story gives you a hint.

activities.title: 拆了重织
activities.story: 隔壁李婶手巧，入秋就把家里的旧毛衣拆了，毛线绕成一个个团。她烧一盆热水，把线团放进去焖一会儿，再捞出来晾干。弯弯曲曲的线变直了，绕在竹针上，又织成一件新的。
activities.story_en: Auntie Li next door had clever hands. At the start of autumn she unravelled the old sweaters at home and wound the yarn into balls. She heated a basin of water, let the balls steep in it for a while, then fished them out to dry. The kinked yarn came out straight; wound onto bamboo needles, it became a new sweater.
activities.prompt: 李婶为什么先用热水把毛线焖一下？
activities.prompt_en: Why did Auntie Li steep the yarn in hot water first?
options_en: To straighten the kinked yarn so it knits easily
To make the yarn stronger
To wash the old colour out
activities.explanation: 拆下来的线是弯的，热水一焖就直了；线顺了，织出来才平整好看。
activities.explanation_en: Unravelled yarn comes off kinked, and hot water relaxes it straight. Smooth yarn knits up flat and neat.
activities.wrong_hint: 那团线后来的变化，就是答案。
activities.wrong_hint_en: Look at what happened to the yarn afterwards.

activities.title: 腊月里的香肠
activities.story: 一进腊月，院子里就挂起一排排香肠。北风一吹，油亮亮的，闻着就香。孩子们仰着头数，数着数着就数不清了，只记得离过年又近了一天。
activities.story_en: As soon as the twelfth lunar month began, rows of sausages hung across the yard. The north wind blew, they shone with fat, and the smell alone was a treat. The children counted them with their heads tipped back, lost count, and only remembered that New Year was one day nearer.
activities.prompt: 香肠为什么要挂在通风的北风里？
activities.prompt_en: Why were the sausages hung out in the draughty north wind?
options_en: So the wind dries them and they keep
So the smell carries further
So the cat cannot reach them
activities.explanation: 腊月里风干冷，挂在通风处慢慢吹干，香肠才不容易坏，味道也更香。
activities.explanation_en: In the twelfth month the wind is cold and dry. Hung in the draught, the sausages dry slowly, keep well, and taste even better.
activities.wrong_hint: 那阵北风是做什么用的，故事里说了。
activities.wrong_hint_en: Think about what that north wind was doing.

activities.title: 大梁上的位子
activities.story: 那时候家里有一辆二八自行车，父亲每天骑车送我上学。我坐在前面的大梁上，他用围巾把我连脖子带脸裹住，只露出两只眼睛。风从耳边过，我一点也不觉得冷。
activities.story_en: Back then the family had a big 28-inch bicycle, and my father rode me to school on it every day. I sat on the crossbar in front, and he wrapped his scarf around my neck and face until only my eyes showed. The wind rushed past my ears, and I was not cold at all.
activities.prompt: 父亲为什么用围巾把孩子裹起来？
activities.prompt_en: Why did he wrap the child up in his scarf?
options_en: To block the wind and keep warm
To keep the road dust off
So the classmates would not see
activities.explanation: 骑车迎着风，风直往领口里钻；围巾一裹，脸和脖子就暖和了。
activities.explanation_en: Riding into the wind, the cold gets straight down your collar. A scarf around the face and neck keeps the warmth in.
activities.wrong_hint: 孩子最后说一点也不冷，这里头有提示。
activities.wrong_hint_en: The child says at the end that they were not cold — there is a hint in that.

activities.title: 家里常做的那道菜
activities.title_en: The dish that was always on the table
activities.prompt: 小时候，家里最常做的一道菜是什么？
activities.prompt_en: When you were small, what dish did your family cook most often?
options_en: A pot of stewed vegetables
A plate of scrambled eggs
Pickles with congee
None of these — it was something else
replies: 一锅炖菜最实在，灶上咕嘟着，屋里都是热乎气。那时候锅里常放白菜，还是土豆？
炒鸡蛋香得很。那时候鸡蛋金贵，能吃上一盘算有口福。您家是拿大葱炒的吗？
咸菜配粥，清清爽爽，早上来一碗最熨帖。您家腌的是萝卜，还是芥菜？
那也一定有它的味道。您说说看，我听着呢。
replies_en: A pot of stew is honest food — bubbling on the stove, filling the room with warmth. What went in most often, cabbage or potatoes?
Scrambled eggs smell wonderful. Eggs were precious then; a plate of them was a real treat. Did your family fry them with spring onion?
Pickles with congee — clean and light, just the thing to start the morning. What did your family pickle, radish or mustard greens?
Then it had a taste of its own. Tell me about it — I'm listening.

activities.title: 夏天的晚上
activities.prompt: 年轻时候的夏天，晚上一般怎么过？
activities.prompt_en: On summer evenings when you were younger, how did you usually spend the time?
options_en: Take a stool out to the yard to cool off
Walk over to the neighbours with a palm fan
Turn the light off early and rest
None of these — it was something else
replies: 院里乘凉最好，一把蒲扇，一张竹床，抬头就是星星。您家院子里种着什么？
摇着蒲扇串门，一坐就是半宿，话比风还多。那时候街坊里谁最爱说笑？
早早歇下也好，第二天还得早起。那时候夏天屋里闷不闷？
那您那时候的晚上是什么样的？说来听听。
replies_en: Cooling off in the yard is the best — a palm fan, a bamboo bed, and stars overhead. What grew in your yard?
Fanning yourself at a neighbour's door, sitting half the night, with more talk than breeze. Who was the biggest talker among the neighbours?
Resting early is sensible too — the next day started early. Was it stuffy indoors in summer?
So what were those evenings like for you? Tell me.

activities.title: 家里的宝贝
activities.prompt: 那时候，家里最值钱的一件东西是什么？
activities.prompt_en: Back then, what was the most valuable thing in your home?
options_en: A sewing machine
A bicycle
A radio
None of these — it was something else
replies: 缝纫机可是个宝贝，踩起来嗒嗒响，一家人的衣裳都从它手底下出来。是蝴蝶牌的吗？
自行车金贵，擦得锃亮，出门办事、接送人都靠它。您家那辆是什么牌子的？
收音机一开，屋里就热闹了，评书、戏曲都在里头。您那时候爱听哪一段？
那一定也是个宝贝。您说说，是什么？
replies_en: A sewing machine was a treasure — ticking away, with the whole family's clothes coming out from under it. Was it a Butterfly?
A bicycle was precious, polished bright, and did every errand and every school run. What make was yours?
Switch the radio on and the room came alive — storytelling, opera, all of it. What did you like listening to?
Then it must have been a treasure too. Tell me, what was it?

activities.title: 过年的盼头
activities.title_en: What you waited for at New Year
activities.prompt: 那时候过年，最盼着的是什么？
activities.prompt_en: Back then, what did you look forward to most at New Year?
options_en: A meal with meat
A new set of clothes
Setting off firecrackers
None of these — it was something else
replies: 一顿有肉的饭，一年到头就盼这一口。您家过年桌上必有的一道菜是什么？
新衣裳要留到初一早上才穿，头天晚上都舍不得睡。是家里做的，还是扯布找人做的？
鞭炮一响，年就到了。您敢自己点吗，还是站在门口看别人放？
那您最盼的是什么？说来听听。
replies_en: A meal with meat — the one thing you waited all year for. What dish was always on your New Year table?
New clothes had to wait until the first morning of the year; the night before, you could hardly sleep. Were they made at home, or by a tailor from cloth you bought?
Once the firecrackers went off, the New Year had arrived. Did you dare light them yourself, or did you watch from the doorway?
So what did you look forward to most? Tell me.

activities.title: 手上的一门活
activities.prompt: 针线、吃食、修修补补，您最拿手的是哪一样？
activities.prompt_en: Sewing, cooking, mending things — which one were you best at?
options_en: Soles and sewing
Dumplings and steamed buns
Mending small things
None really — I watched others do it
replies: 纳鞋底、缝衣裳，针脚匀不匀，一看就知道手上的功夫。您给谁做过？
和面、发面、上锅，一样都省不得。您蒸的馒头是不是又白又暄？
会修东西的人，街坊都爱找。您修过最得意的一样是什么？
看着别人做，也是热闹日子的一部分。您最喜欢看谁做？
replies_en: Soles and sewing — even stitches show the skill in your hands. Who did you make things for?
Mixing, proving, steaming — none of it can be skipped. Were your steamed buns white and fluffy?
People who can mend things are always in demand. What was the repair you were proudest of?
Watching others make things is part of a lively home too. Whose work did you most like to watch?

activities.title: 上门做客
activities.prompt: 那时候去亲戚家串门，主人家一般端出什么招待？
activities.prompt_en: When you visited relatives back then, what would the host bring out?
options_en: A bowl of sugar water
A handful of melon seeds
A cup of hot tea
Some other little snack
replies: 一碗糖水，甜到心里，那时候糖还要凭票。是白糖水，还是放了红枣？
一把瓜子，边嗑边说话，壳堆成小山。您嗑瓜子快不快？
一杯热茶端上来，先暖手再暖心。您家来客人的时候泡的是什么茶？
各家的讲究不一样，端出来的都是心意。您那时最爱上谁家做客？
replies_en: A bowl of sugar water, sweet right through — sugar was rationed then. Plain, or with red dates in it?
A handful of melon seeds, cracked while talking, shells piling up like a little hill. Were you quick at cracking them?
A cup of hot tea warms your hands first, then your heart. What tea did your family make for guests?
Every family had its own way, and every one was a kindness. Whose home did you most like visiting?

activities.title: 家门口的样子
activities.title_en: The doorway you grew up with
activities.prompt: 小时候住的地方，家门口是什么样子？
activities.prompt_en: The place where you grew up — what was the doorway like?
options_en: A dirt road
A few stone steps
A big tree
None of these — it was something else
replies: 土路一下雨就泥，鞋上沾一圈泥。您小时候下雨天怎么出门？
石阶被踩得发亮，门槛也磨圆了。那时候门口常坐着谁？
门口有棵树最好，夏天遮阴，秋天落叶。是什么树，还记得吗？
那您家门口是什么样子的？慢慢说，我听着。
replies_en: A dirt road turns to mud in the rain and leaves a ring on your shoes. How did you get about on rainy days?
Stone steps worn shiny, a threshold rounded by feet. Who used to sit by the door?
A tree by the door is the best — shade in summer, leaves in autumn. Do you remember what kind it was?
So what was your doorway like? Take your time — I'm listening.
